arxiv-2109-03865.title: Transport-Enabled Entangling Gate for Trapped Ions
arxiv-2109-03865.creator: Holly N. Tinkey, Craig R. Clark, Brian C. Sawyer, Kenton R. Brown
arxiv-2109-03865.description: Abstract We implement a 2-qubit entangling Mølmer-Sørensen interaction by transporting two cotrapped Ca + 40 {}^{40}\mathrm{Ca}^{+} ions through a stationary, bichromatic optical beam within a surface-electrode Paul trap. We describe a procedure for achieving a constant Doppler shift during the transport which uses fine temporal adjustment of the moving confinement potential.

arxiv-2112-03274.title: Fast verification of spent nuclear fuel dry casks using cosmic ray muons: Monte Carlo simulation study
arxiv-2112-03274.creator: A.Sh. Georgadze
arxiv-2112-03274.description: Abstract An application of muon scattering tomography is investigated for the non-destructive verification of spent nuclear fuel dry storage casks in context of international treaty declarations in proving that the diversion of plutonium has not occurred during long term storage in the spent fuel storage facility.

arxiv-2210-04502.title: A Reunion of Gödel, Tarski, Carnap , and Rosser
arxiv-2210-04502.creator: Saeed Salehi Department of Mathematics, Statistics, and Computer Science, University of Tabriz, Bahman 29 t ​ h {}^{\,th} Boulevard, P.O.Box 51666–16471, Tabriz, IRAN. E-mail:​ salehipour@tabrizu.ac.ir
arxiv-2210-04502.description: Abstract We unify Gödel ’s First Incompleteness Theorem (1931), Tarski ’s Undefinability Theorem (1933), Gödel-Carnap ’s Diagonal Lemma (1934), and Rosser ’s (strengthening of Gödel ’s first) Incompleteness Theorem (1936), whose proofs resemble much and use almost the same technique.

arxiv-2301-04053.title: Coffee stain effect on a fibre from axisymmetric droplets
arxiv-2301-04053.creator: Marie Corpart 1, Frédéric Restagno 1, François Boulogne 1
arxiv-2301-04053.description: Abstract The so-called coffee stain effect has been intensively studied over the past decades, but most of the studies are focused on sessile droplets. In this paper, we analyse the origin of the difference between the deposition of suspended particles in a sessile drop and in an axisymmetric drop deposited on a fibre.

arxiv-2301-05241.title: Debiasing Standard Siren Inference of the Hubble Constant with Marginal Neural Ratio Estimation 2022 Debiasing Standard Siren Inference of the Hubble Constant with Marginal Neural Ratio Estimation – A.4
arxiv-2301-05241.creator: Samuel Gagnon-Hartman, John Ruan, Daryl Haggard
arxiv-2301-05241.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Samuel Gagnon-Hartman, John Ruan, Daryl Haggard. Gravitational wave (GW) standard sirens may resolve the Hubble tension, provided that standard siren inference of H 0 H_{0} is free from systematic biases. However, standard sirens from binary neutron star (BNS) mergers suffer from two sources of systematic bias, one arising from the anisotropy of GW emission, and the other from the anisotropy of electromagnetic (EM) emission from the kilonova.

arxiv-2307-09513.title: Probing the Conditions for the H i -to-H 2 Transition in the Interstellar Medium Journal: ApJ
arxiv-2307-09513.creator: Gyueun Park, Min-Young Lee, Shmuel Bialy, Blakesley Burkhart, J. R. Dawson, Carl Heiles, Di Li, Claire Murray, Hiep Nguyen, Anita Hafner, Daniel R. Rybarczyk, Snežana Stanimirović
arxiv-2307-09513.description: Abstract In this paper, we investigate the conditions for the H i -to-H 2 transition in the solar neighborhood by analyzing H i emission and absorption measurements toward 58 Galactic lines of sight (LOSs) along with 12 CO(1–0) (CO) and dust data.

arxiv-2312-09814.title: Review of Hubble tension solutions with new SH0ES and SPT-3G data
arxiv-2312-09814.creator: Karim Benabed
arxiv-2312-09814.description: Abstract We present an updated analysis of eleven cosmological models that may help reduce the Hubble tension, which now reaches the 6 ​ σ 6\sigma level when considering the latest SH0ES measurement versus recent CMB and BAO data, assuming Λ \Lambda CDM.

pmc-11312481.title: Comparative Analysis of Ketorolac and Parecoxib for Postoperative Pain Management in Uvulopalatopharyngoplasty
pmc-11312481.creator: Cheng-Yu Hsieh, Chuan-Hung Sun, Chung-Ching Lin, Yi-Fan Chou, Eng Ooi, Ralph Mösges
pmc-11312481.description: Background/Objectives: Uvulopalatopharyngoplasty (UPPP) is a prevalent surgical procedure for treating obstructive sleep apnea. Effective postoperative pain management is crucial for patient comfort and recovery. This study aimed to compare the analgesic efficacies of parecoxib and ketorolac in patients undergoing UPPP.

pmc-11341034.title: The effects of different music types on tennis performance among recreational players
pmc-11341034.creator: Furkan Cengiz, Ozkan Isik, Zlatan Bilic, Dario Novak
pmc-11341034.description: It is known that different types of music used during sports performance has different psycho-physiological effects. In this context, this study aimed to reveal the effect of different types of music on ITN test performance in tennis players. A total of 35 recreational tennis players voluntarily participated in the study.

pmc-11429125.title: Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) Changes in Virologically Suppressed People Living with HIVSwitching to Long-Acting Cabotegravir and Rilpivirine
pmc-11429125.creator: Nicolò De Gennaro, Mariacristina Poliseno, Angelo Dargenio, Flavia Balena, Deborah Fiordelisi, Vito Spada, Greta Romita, Giacomo Guido, Francesco Di Gennaro, Giuseppe Bruno, Mariantonietta Purgatorio, Giovanni Battista Buccoliero, Annalisa Saracino, Adriana Pistol
pmc-11429125.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: Limited evidence is available about sleep quality changes associated with the use of Cabotegravir (CAB), a new, long-acting (LA) antiretroviral (ARV) drug belonging to the class of Integrase Strand Transfer Inhibitors (INSTIs). Methods: Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) was calculated in 53 people living with HIV (PLWH) under the care of the outpatient services of two Italian Infectious Diseases Centers in Apuliabefore (M0) and seven months after (M7) the switch to LA CAB.

pmc-11799273.title: A dosimetric comparison of non-coplanar volumetric modulated arc therapy and non-coplanar fixed field intensity modulated radiation therapy in hippocampus-avoidance whole-brain radiation therapy with a simultaneous integrated boost for brain metastases
pmc-11799273.creator: Huaqu Zeng, MinZhi Zhong, Zongyou Chen, Shukui Tang, Zunbei Wen
pmc-11799273.description: ObjectiveThe aim of this study was to investigate the dosimetric differences between non-coplanar volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT) and non-coplanar fixed-field intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT) in hippocampus-avoidance whole-brain radiation therapy with a simultaneous integrated boost (HA-WBRT+SIB) for brain metastases using the Monaco treatment planning system (TPS).MethodA total of 22 patients with brain metastases were retrospectively enrolled.

pmc-13127131.title: ROS-responsive drug delivery systems for chronic wound healing: advances, challenges, and translational perspectives
pmc-13127131.creator: Yuan Xiong, Qi-Peng Wu, Han Wang, Mohammad-Ali Shahbazi, Bo-Bin Mi
pmc-13127131.description: Chronic wounds pose a substantial global health burden, due to the high incidence and recurrence rates, and associated morbidity. Excessive and sustained production of reactive oxygen species (ROS) is a hallmark of the chronic wound microenvironment, ultimately stalling the repair process.

pmc-13360455.title: Monitoring Animal Poisoning in Central Italy: Long-Term Trends and Spatial Distribution in the Abruzzo Region
pmc-13360455.creator: Antonio Petrini, Alice Menozzi, Carmine Merola, Giampiero Scortichini, Daria Di Sabatino, Luca Brugnola, Stefania Salucci, Elga Ersilia Tieri, Daniela Averaimo, Antonio Cocco, Giorgio Saluti, Giuseppe Gatti, Rachele Rocchi, Davide De Tiberis, Maria Laura Marchetti, Daniel Buldain, Pedro Zeinsteger,
pmc-13360455.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Simple SummaryThe poisoning of domestic and wild animals—whether accidental, deliberate, or unlawful—is a well-documented phenomenon in the global literature and continues to represent a significant risk for humans, animals, and the environment. In the present study, we investigated the temporal and spatial distribution of animal carcasses and suspected poisoned baits collected in the Abruzzo region, located in central Italy, and submitted to a public veterinary institute for necropsy, inspection, and toxicological analyses.

pmc-13440100.title: Acute kidney injury and mortality in cirrhosis: a nationwide analysis of clinical outcomes, resource utilization, and effect modification
pmc-13440100.creator: Brent Tai, Chijioke Okonkwo, Arturo Riviera
pmc-13440100.description: BackgroundAcute kidney injury (AKI) is a common complication in patients with cirrhosis and is associated with poor outcomes. However, contemporary national data quantifying the impact of AKI severity on mortality and healthcare utilization, as well as potential effect modification across patient subgroups, remain limited.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective cohort study using the 2023 Nationwide Inpatient Sample.
